# Analysis overview

This extends from the preivous co-acessibility analysis in `/project/spott/cshan/fiber-seq/code/co-accessibility/LCL/LCL_co-access.Rmd`
I preivously used Fisher exact to test if the CRE pairs are more often co-accessible than expected, but there is high donor heterogeneity,
the CRE pairs accessible in one donor may not be accessible in another. This might be a problem because:

  - mixing donor creates an assoication

Permutation test shuffles CRE2 m6A proportions only within each sample. 
Each shuffled dataset keeps every sample's own CRE1 and CRE2 distributions, so any correlation caused by sample-level differences is also 
present in the null. The only thing the shuffle breaks is which CRE1 value sits on the same fiber as which CRE2 value



The `pooled` analysis includes all 31 samples and the `noXCI` analysis uses the existing noXCI results and sex assignments: chrX uses male samples 
only, and all other chromosomes use all 31 samples 

Accessibility comes from `label_reads(read_rule = "contain",
fire_overlap_fraction = 0.5)` applied to `load_region(span_source =
"aligned_blocks")`. Only `shared == TRUE` fibers enter methylation summaries.
Sample counts are read from `LCL_pair_sample_counts.tsv.gz`; donor bars and
observed/expected summaries use those original counts, before methylation filtering.

For each original cCRE, `assemble_region_m6a(full_span = TRUE, positions = NULL)`
builds **one pooled read × position matrix** for the included samples. Its existing
tabix reader keeps the longest overlapping alignment per read, removes sentinel
blocks, and records binary m6A calls. The denominator is **the number of matrix
columns**, i.e. positions with at least one observed m6A call among those pooled
full-span reads. It is not a count of reference adenines or informative adenines.
The column set is fixed before matching to Fisher fibers and is retained for all
pooled, FIRE-state, and donor summaries; columns are not dropped after filtering.
Full-span reads with zero calls remain zero rows.

For each matched fiber, `prop1 = rowSums(CRE1_matrix) / ncol(CRE1_matrix)` and
`prop2 = rowSums(CRE2_matrix) / ncol(CRE2_matrix)`. Main means and correlations
use Fisher fibers present in **both** matrices. The per-fiber export also retains
every Fisher fiber, with any available single-cCRE proportion and explicit
exclusion reasons, so attrition can be inspected. Missing records are not zeros.
BED cCRE starts are converted to 1-based starts only when calling the existing
matrix API; the biological intervals are unchanged.

```{r settings}
coaccess_dir <- file.path(params$root, "coaccess")
universe_dir <- file.path(params$root, "universe")
analysis_sets <- c("pooled", "noXCI")
stopifnot(params$n_permutations == 10000L)
state_columns <- c("co_access", "CRE1_access", "CRE2_access", "co_closed")
state_labels <- setNames(CONFIG_LEVELS, state_columns)
read_rule <- "contain"
fire_overlap_fraction <- 0.5

# Save only final processed TSVs and PDFs, directly in the requested folders.
out_dir <- file.path(params$root, "co-access_v2_perm_methy_prop")
table_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "tables")
plot_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "plots")
for (d in c(table_dir, plot_dir)) dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
if (length(list.files(table_dir)) || length(list.files(plot_dir)))
  stop("Output folders already contain results; refusing to overwrite: ", out_dir)
write_table <- function(x, name) {
  path <- file.path(table_dir, name)
  if (file.exists(path)) stop("Refusing to overwrite ", path)
  fwrite(x, path, sep = "\t", na = "NA")
  invisible(path)
}
final_plots <- list()
queue_plot <- function(p, name, width = 13, height = 10) {
  final_plots[[name]] <<- list(plot = p, width = width, height = height)
}
cat("Results directory:", out_dir, "\n")
```

```{r validate-inputs}
sample_meta <- fread(params$sample_sheet)
manifest <- fread(file.path(universe_dir, "sample_manifest.tsv"))

stopifnot(nrow(sample_meta) == 31L, nrow(manifest) == 31L,
          nrow(run_manifest) == 31L,
          !anyDuplicated(sample_meta$sample_name), !anyDuplicated(manifest$sample_name),
          !anyDuplicated(run_manifest$sample_name),
          setequal(sample_meta$sample_name, manifest$sample_name),
          setequal(run_manifest$sample_name, manifest$sample_name))
samples <- as.character(manifest$sample_name)
sample_meta <- sample_meta[match(samples, sample_name)]
sample_meta[, donor := as.character(cell_line)]
run_manifest <- run_manifest[match(samples, sample_name)]
stopifnot(identical(as.character(manifest$donor), sample_meta$donor))
provenance_columns <- c("sample_name", "donor", "fire_dir", "cram_path",
                        "elements_path", "spans_path")
for (column in provenance_columns) {
  if (!identical(as.character(run_manifest[[column]]), as.character(manifest[[column]])))
    stop("Universe and completed-run manifests differ in ", column)
}
same_paths <- function(a, b)
  identical(normalizePath(a, mustWork = TRUE), normalizePath(b, mustWork = TRUE))
stopifnot(same_paths(manifest$fire_dir, file.path(params$fire_root, samples)),
          same_paths(run_manifest$blocks_path,
            file.path(params$root, samples, paste0(samples, ".aligned_blocks.bed.gz"))),

donors <- unique(sample_meta$donor)
male_samples <- character()
if ("noXCI" %in% analysis_sets) {
  sex_noxci <- fread(file.path(coaccess_dir, "noXCI", "LCL_sample_sex_noXCI.tsv"))
  stopifnot(nrow(sex_noxci) == 31L, !anyDuplicated(sex_noxci$sample_name),
            setequal(sex_noxci$sample_name, samples),
            all(sex_noxci$sex %in% c("male (XY)", "female (XX)")),
            identical(as.character(sex_noxci$donor[match(samples, sex_noxci$sample_name)]),
                      sample_meta$donor))
  male_samples <- samples[samples %in% sex_noxci[sex == "male (XY)", sample_name]]
  stopifnot(length(male_samples) > 0L)
}
```

# Load the top-ten pairs

Both top-ten sets are loaded from the tables saved by `LCL/LCL_co-access.Rmd`
in `coaccess/`: `LCL_top10_pairs.tsv` (pooled) and `LCL_top10_pairs_noXCI.tsv`
(noXCI). Their pair IDs and 1,000-bp aligned-block loading windows are used
unchanged. m6A matrices always use the original cCRE boundaries. Saved Fisher
columns are exported unchanged; no donor Fisher tests are added.

```{r load-top-ten}
top10_files <- c(pooled = file.path(coaccess_dir, "LCL_top10_pairs.tsv"),
                 noXCI = file.path(coaccess_dir, "LCL_top10_pairs_noXCI.tsv"))
selected_sets <- setNames(lapply(analysis_sets, function(a) {
  chosen <- fread(top10_files[[a]])
  chosen[, `:=`(analysis = a, pair_rank = seq_len(.N))]
  chosen
}), analysis_sets)
selected <- rbindlist(selected_sets, fill = TRUE)
selected[, .(analysis, pair_rank, pair_id, CRE_pair, gene_names)]
```

```{r original-sample-counts}
# Stream the large file once, retaining only the selected pairs.
read_selected_counts <- function(path, pair_ids) {
  con <- gzfile(path, "rt")
  on.exit(close(con))
  header <- readLines(con, n = 1L)
  out <- list()
  repeat {
    lines <- readLines(con, n = 100000L)
    if (!length(lines)) break
    ids <- substr(lines, 1L, regexpr("\t", lines, fixed = TRUE) - 1L)
    lines <- lines[ids %in% pair_ids]
    if (length(lines)) out[[length(out) + 1L]] <-
      fread(text = paste(c(header, lines), collapse = "\n"), sep = "\t")
  }
  rbindlist(out)
}
counts_file <- file.path(coaccess_dir, "LCL_pair_sample_counts.tsv.gz")
sample_counts <- read_selected_counts(counts_file, unique(selected$CRE_pair))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(sample_counts[, .(CRE_pair, sample_name)]),
          all(sample_counts$sample_name %in% samples),
          all(sample_counts$donor == sample_meta$donor[match(sample_counts$sample_name, samples)]),
          all(rowSums(as.matrix(sample_counts[, ..state_columns])) == sample_counts$n_shared_reads))
pair_samples_for <- function(pair) {
  if (pair$analysis == "noXCI" && pair$chrom == "chrX") male_samples else samples
}
counts_for <- function(pair) {
  included <- pair_samples_for(pair)
  z <- sample_counts[CRE_pair == pair$CRE_pair & sample_name %in% included]
  stopifnot(nrow(z) == length(included), setequal(z$sample_name, included),
            all(z$chrom == pair$chrom))
  z <- copy(z[match(included, sample_name)])
  suffix <- if (pair$analysis == "noXCI") "_noXCI" else ""
  for (column in c(state_columns, "n_shared_reads"))
    if (sum(z[[column]]) != pair[[paste0(column, suffix)]])
      stop("Saved sample counts disagree with pooled Fisher table: ", pair$pair_id, " / ", column)
  z[, `:=`(analysis = pair$analysis, pair_id = pair$pair_id, pair_rank = pair$pair_rank)]
  z
}
selected_sample_counts <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(selected)), function(i) counts_for(selected[i])))
```

# Donor accessibility

For each donor, observed co-accessibility is `co_access`; expected co-accessibility
under independence is `(co_access + CRE1_access) * (co_access + CRE2_access) / N`,
where `N` is the donor's total shared fibers. Fractions divide these counts by `N`.
These descriptive values use unmodified counts without pseudocounts. A donor with
zero shared fibers has undefined fractions and is labelled `n=0` without a bar.

```{r donor-accessibility-summary}
donor_accessibility <- selected_sample_counts[, lapply(.SD, sum),
  by = .(analysis, pair_id, pair_rank, CRE_pair, donor),
  .SDcols = c(state_columns, "n_shared_reads")]
donor_accessibility[, `:=`(
  observed_co_access = co_access,
  expected_co_access = fifelse(n_shared_reads > 0,
    expected_coaccess(co_closed, CRE1_access, CRE2_access, co_access), NA_real_))]
donor_accessibility[, `:=`(
  observed_fraction = fifelse(n_shared_reads > 0, co_access / n_shared_reads, NA_real_),
  expected_fraction = fifelse(n_shared_reads > 0, expected_co_access / n_shared_reads, NA_real_),
  observed_expected_ratio = fifelse(expected_co_access > 0, co_access / expected_co_access, NA_real_))]
for (state in state_columns)
  donor_accessibility[, (paste0(state, "_fraction")) :=
    fifelse(n_shared_reads > 0, get(state) / n_shared_reads, NA_real_)]
donor_states <- melt(donor_accessibility,
  id.vars = c("analysis", "pair_id", "pair_rank", "CRE_pair", "donor", "n_shared_reads"),
  measure.vars = state_columns, variable.name = "state", value.name = "n_fibers")
donor_states[, `:=`(config = factor(state_labels[as.character(state)], levels = CONFIG_LEVELS),
                    fraction = fifelse(n_shared_reads > 0, n_fibers / n_shared_reads, NA_real_))]
```

```{r donor-accessibility-bars, fig.height=12}
if (isTRUE(params$make_plots)) for (a in analysis_sets) {
  d <- copy(donor_states[analysis == a])
  d[, donor := factor(donor, levels = donors)]
  d[, pair_id := factor(pair_id, levels = selected_sets[[a]]$pair_id)]
  totals <- unique(d[, .(pair_id, donor, n_shared_reads)])
  totals[, lab := paste0("n=", n_shared_reads)]
  p <- plot_stacked_proportion(d[n_shared_reads > 0], "donor", "config", CONFIG_COLS,
    y = "fraction", position = "stack",
    totals = list(data = totals, x = "donor", y = 1.03, label = "lab",
                  style = list(size = 2.3, angle = 90, hjust = 0)),
    scales = list(scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(),
                                    breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1), limits = c(0, 1.25)),
                  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE)),
    labels = list(x = NULL, y = "Fraction of shared fibers", title = paste(a, "- donor FIRE accessibility")),
    legend = list(name = NULL, drop = FALSE),
    theme = theme_fiberseq("bw", base_size = 10,
      overrides = list(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1),
                       legend.position = "bottom"))) + facet_wrap(~pair_id, ncol = 2)
  print(p)
  queue_plot(p, paste0(a, "_donor_accessibility"), height = 12)
}
```

# Matrix proportions and exclusion audit

The additional metadata query below uses the same existing `read_ft_bed12()`
reader and longest-alignment rule solely to explain exclusions. It does not call
methylation or construct a second matrix. The matrix itself always comes from
`assemble_region_m6a()`. Missing inputs and inconsistent identities stop the run.
The existing parser also stops if a cCRE has fewer than three full-span reads or
no observed m6A positions. Audits and matrix checks stay in memory; final fiber
and exclusion tables report any filtering.

```{r methylation-helpers}
matrix_proportions <- function(pair, cre_number, fisher_fibers, included) {
  region <- data.frame(region_id = paste0(pair$pair_id, "_CRE", cre_number),
    chr = pair$chrom, start = pair[[paste0("cre", cre_number, "_start")]],
    end = pair[[paste0("cre", cre_number, "_end")]])
  region$analysis_start <- region$start + 1L
  region$analysis_end <- region$end
  st <- sample_table[match(included, sample_table$sample_name), , drop = FALSE]
  paths <- file.path(st$fire_dir, "extracted_results", "m6a_by_chr",
    paste0(st$sample_name, ".ft_extracted_m6a.", region$chr, ".bed.gz"))
  required <- c(paths, paste0(paths, ".tbi"))
  if (!all(file.exists(required))) stop("Missing m6A input/index: ", paste(required[!file.exists(required)], collapse = ", "))
  gr <- GenomicRanges::GRanges(region$chr, IRanges::IRanges(region$analysis_start, region$analysis_end))
  # Record spans before full_span filtering, including overlapping zero-call reads.
  audit_records <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_along(included), function(j) {
    b <- read_ft_bed12(paths[j], region = gr, longest_alignment = TRUE)
    if (!nrow(b)) return(data.table(sample_name = character(), original_RID = character(),
                                   ft_start = integer(), ft_end = integer(), full_span = logical()))
    data.table(sample_name = included[j], original_RID = as.character(b$RID),
      ft_start = b$start, ft_end = b$end,
      full_span = b$start <= region$start & b$end >= region$end)
  }))
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(audit_records[, .(sample_name, original_RID)]))
  audit <- merge(fisher_fibers[, .(sample_name, original_RID, donor, state)],
    audit_records, by = c("sample_name", "original_RID"), all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
  audit[, status := fifelse(is.na(full_span), "missing_ft_record",
                            fifelse(full_span, "retained", "excluded_full_span"))]
  audit[, `:=`(analysis = pair$analysis, pair_id = pair$pair_id,
               CRE_pair = pair$CRE_pair, CRE = paste0("CRE", cre_number))]

  assembled <- assemble_region_m6a(st, region, modality = "m6a",
    full_span = TRUE, positions = NULL, matrix_dir = NULL, reuse = FALSE)
  mat <- assembled$met_mat
  meta <- as.data.table(assembled$rids_df)
  positions <- as.integer(colnames(mat))
  stopifnot(identical(rownames(mat), as.character(meta$RID)),
            !anyDuplicated(meta[, .(sample_name, original_RID)]),
            identical(meta$RID, paste(meta$sample_name, meta$original_RID, sep = "::")),
            ncol(mat) > 0L, !anyNA(mat), all(mat@x %in% c(0, 1)),
            !anyNA(positions), !anyDuplicated(positions),
            identical(positions, sort(positions)),
            all(positions >= region$analysis_start & positions <= region$analysis_end),
            all(Matrix::colSums(mat) > 0),
            all(meta$start <= region$analysis_start & meta$end >= region$analysis_end),
            nrow(meta) == sum(audit_records$full_span))
  expected_ids <- audit_records[full_span == TRUE, paste(sample_name, original_RID, sep = "::")]
  stopifnot(setequal(meta$RID, expected_ids))

  # Subset rows only: every sample/state/donor retains this exact column set.
  rows <- match(paste(audit$sample_name, audit$original_RID, sep = "::"), meta$RID)
  present <- !is.na(rows)
  stopifnot(identical(present, audit$status == "retained"))
  matched_mat <- mat[rows[present], , drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(identical(colnames(matched_mat), colnames(mat)))
  audit[, `:=`(n_m6a_calls = NA_real_, proportion = NA_real_, n_positions = ncol(mat))]
  audit[present, `:=`(n_m6a_calls = as.numeric(Matrix::rowSums(matched_mat)),
                     proportion = as.numeric(Matrix::rowSums(matched_mat)) / ncol(mat))]
  stopifnot(all(audit$proportion[present] >= 0 & audit$proportion[present] <= 1))

  qc <- as.data.table(assembled$qc)
  qc[, `:=`(analysis = pair$analysis, pair_id = pair$pair_id,
            CRE = paste0("CRE", cre_number), n_positions = ncol(mat),
            excluded_full_span_reads = overlapping_reads - full_span_reads)]
  checks <- data.table(analysis = pair$analysis, pair_id = pair$pair_id,
    CRE = paste0("CRE", cre_number), n_positions = ncol(mat),
    n_matrix_reads = nrow(mat), n_shared_matrix_reads = nrow(matched_mat),
    consistent_columns = identical(colnames(mat), colnames(matched_mat)),
    binary_matrix = TRUE, positions_observed_in_pooled_matrix = TRUE)
  list(fibers = audit, qc = qc, checks = checks)
}
```

```{r calculate-all-fiber-proportions}
fiber_results <- matrix_qc <- matrix_checks <- span_audits <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(selected))) {
  pair <- selected[i]
  included <- pair_samples_for(pair)
  message("Analysing ", pair$analysis, " / ", pair$pair_id)
  res <- load_region(list(chrom = pair$chrom, start = pair$region_start, end = pair$region_end),
    included, params$root, params$fire_root, fire_ver = "v0.1",
    tabix_bin = params$tabix, span_source = "aligned_blocks")
  labels <- label_reads(res,
    list(start = pair$cre1_start, end = pair$cre1_end),
    list(start = pair$cre2_start, end = pair$cre2_end),
    read_rule = read_rule, fire_overlap_fraction = fire_overlap_fraction)
  identity <- res$spans[, .(key, sample_name, original_RID = as.character(RID))]
  fibers <- merge(labels[shared == TRUE], identity,
                  by = c("key", "sample_name"), all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
  stopifnot(!anyNA(fibers$original_RID),
            !anyDuplicated(fibers[, .(sample_name, original_RID)]), all(fibers$shared))
  fibers[, `:=`(donor = sample_meta$donor[match(sample_name, samples)],
    state = fifelse(acc1 & acc2, "co_access", fifelse(acc1, "CRE1_access",
                    fifelse(acc2, "CRE2_access", "co_closed"))))]
  actual <- fibers[, .(co_access = sum(acc1 & acc2), CRE1_access = sum(acc1 & !acc2),
    CRE2_access = sum(!acc1 & acc2), co_closed = sum(!acc1 & !acc2), n_shared_reads = .N),
    by = sample_name]
  original <- counts_for(pair)
  for (column in c(state_columns, "n_shared_reads")) {
    values <- actual[[column]][match(original$sample_name, actual$sample_name)]
    values[is.na(values)] <- 0L
    if (!identical(as.numeric(values), as.numeric(original[[column]])))
      stop("Reloaded FIRE counts differ by sample for ", pair$pair_id, " / ", column)
  }
  m1 <- matrix_proportions(pair, 1L, fibers, included)
  m2 <- matrix_proportions(pair, 2L, fibers, included)
  for (j in 1:2) {
    m <- if (j == 1L) m1 else m2
    z <- m$fibers[, .(sample_name, original_RID, status, n_m6a_calls, proportion, n_positions)]
    setnames(z, c("status", "n_m6a_calls", "proportion", "n_positions"),
      c(paste0("CRE", j, "_status"), paste0("m6a_calls", j), paste0("prop", j), paste0("n_positions", j)))
    fibers <- merge(fibers, z, by = c("sample_name", "original_RID"), all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
  }
  fibers[, `:=`(analysis = pair$analysis, pair_id = pair$pair_id, pair_rank = pair$pair_rank,
    CRE_pair = pair$CRE_pair, chrom = pair$chrom,
    qualifying = CRE1_status == "retained" & CRE2_status == "retained" & is.finite(prop1) & is.finite(prop2))]
  setorder(fibers, sample_name, original_RID)
  fiber_results[[i]] <- fibers
  matrix_qc[[i]] <- rbind(m1$qc, m2$qc)
  matrix_checks[[i]] <- rbind(m1$checks, m2$checks)
  span_audits[[i]] <- rbind(m1$fibers, m2$fibers)
}
per_fiber <- rbindlist(fiber_results)
matrix_qc <- rbindlist(matrix_qc)
matrix_checks <- rbindlist(matrix_checks)
span_audit <- rbindlist(span_audits)
exclusions <- per_fiber[, .(n_fisher_fibers = .N, n_qualifying = sum(qualifying),
  n_excluded = sum(!qualifying),
  n_CRE1_full_span_excluded = sum(CRE1_status == "excluded_full_span"),
  n_CRE2_full_span_excluded = sum(CRE2_status == "excluded_full_span"),
  n_either_full_span_excluded = sum(CRE1_status == "excluded_full_span" | CRE2_status == "excluded_full_span"),
  n_CRE1_missing_ft_record = sum(CRE1_status == "missing_ft_record"),
  n_CRE2_missing_ft_record = sum(CRE2_status == "missing_ft_record")),
  by = .(analysis, pair_id, pair_rank, donor, sample_name)]
pair_attrition <- exclusions[, lapply(.SD, sum), by = .(analysis, pair_id, pair_rank),
  .SDcols = setdiff(names(exclusions), c("analysis", "pair_id", "pair_rank", "donor", "sample_name"))]
print(pair_attrition)
print(matrix_checks)
print(matrix_qc[, .(overlapping_reads = sum(overlapping_reads),
                    full_span_reads = sum(full_span_reads),
                    excluded_full_span_reads = sum(excluded_full_span_reads)),
                by = .(analysis, pair_id, CRE)])
```

# Pooled methylation means

Every fiber has equal weight. The four-state and donor summaries partition the
same qualifying fibers used for the pooled means and correlation, using the
same CRE1 and CRE2 denominators. Empty donor/state groups have `n_fibers = 0`
and `NA` means. Donor summaries are descriptive; no donor significance tests run.

```{r methylation-summaries}
# mean_props() and complete_summary() come from stats_testing_functions.r.
qualifying <- per_fiber[qualifying == TRUE]
pair_keys <- c("analysis", "pair_id", "pair_rank", "CRE_pair")
pair_grid <- unique(selected[, ..pair_keys])
pooled_means <- complete_summary(pair_grid, mean_props(qualifying, pair_keys), pair_keys)
state_grid <- pair_grid[, .(state = state_columns), by = pair_keys]
state_keys <- c(pair_keys, "state")
state_means <- complete_summary(state_grid, mean_props(qualifying, state_keys), state_keys)
donor_keys <- c(pair_keys, "donor")
donor_grid <- unique(selected_sample_counts[, ..donor_keys])
donor_means <- complete_summary(donor_grid, mean_props(qualifying, donor_keys), donor_keys)
denominators <- unique(per_fiber[, .(analysis, pair_id, n_positions1, n_positions2)])
stopifnot(nrow(denominators) == nrow(selected))
pooled_means <- merge(pooled_means, denominators, by = c("analysis", "pair_id"))
state_means <- merge(state_means, denominators, by = c("analysis", "pair_id"))
donor_means <- merge(donor_means, denominators, by = c("analysis", "pair_id"))
print(pooled_means[order(analysis, pair_rank)])
```

# Same-fiber correlation and sample-stratified permutations

The primary statistic is Spearman correlation across all qualifying fibers in
a pair. Each of 10,000 permutations shuffles CRE2 proportions **within the same
sample**, while CRE1 proportions and sample identity remain fixed. Global
midranks are computed once: permuting values also permutes their ranks, so the
observed and permuted statistics are the same Spearman statistic, including ties.
The empirical one-sided p-value for positive association is
`(1 + sum(permuted_rho >= observed_rho)) / (10000 + 1)`.
BH correction uses the ten primary tests within each selected analysis set.

Sample differences can produce a positive pooled correlation and a nonzero
permutation-null mean. As an additional statistic, global ranks are centered
within sample and the residual ranks are correlated. This is a sample-adjusted
rank correlation (equivalent to residualizing each global rank against sample
indicators), not an average of per-donor tests. Its supplementary p-values use
the same sample-stratified permutations, with a separate ten-test BH family.
Constant proportions and lack of within-sample variation are explicitly flagged;
undefined correlations remain `NA`. Singleton samples stay in the primary
analysis but their values cannot shuffle. No fibers are downsampled for analysis
or for the scatterplots. Inference is conditional on these accessibility-selected
pairs and is not a genome-wide methylation significance claim.

`permute_pooled_spearman()` is sourced from `stats_testing_functions.r`.

```{r run-permutations}
permutation_results <- permutation_nulls <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(selected))) {
  pair <- selected[i]
  d <- per_fiber[analysis == pair$analysis & pair_id == pair$pair_id & qualifying == TRUE]
  # Seeds depend on analysis and rank, not on which sets run in this invocation.
  pair_seed <- as.integer(params$seed + pair$pair_rank + if (pair$analysis == "noXCI") 1000L else 0L)
  fit <- permute_pooled_spearman(d, n_permutations = params$n_permutations, seed = pair_seed)
  s <- as.data.table(fit$statistics)
  s[, `:=`(analysis = pair$analysis, pair_id = pair$pair_id,
            pair_rank = pair$pair_rank, CRE_pair = pair$CRE_pair)]
  n <- as.data.table(fit$null)
  n[, `:=`(analysis = pair$analysis, pair_id = pair$pair_id, pair_rank = pair$pair_rank)]
  permutation_results[[i]] <- s
  permutation_nulls[[i]] <- n
}
permutation_statistics <- rbindlist(permutation_results)
permutation_null <- rbindlist(permutation_nulls)
permutation_statistics[, `:=`(bh_family_size = 10L,
  p_positive_BH = adjust_bh(p_positive, n = 10L),
  adjusted_p_positive_BH = adjust_bh(adjusted_p_positive, n = 10L)), by = analysis]
permutation_statistics <- merge(permutation_statistics, pair_attrition,
  by = c("analysis", "pair_id", "pair_rank"))
permutation_statistics <- merge(permutation_statistics, denominators, by = c("analysis", "pair_id"))
setorder(permutation_statistics, analysis, pair_rank)
print(permutation_statistics[, .(analysis, pair_id, n_qualifying, spearman_rho,
  p_positive, p_positive_BH, within_sample_adjusted_rho, adjusted_p_positive_BH,
  null_mean, status)])
```

# Empirical permutation p-value diagnostics

Kevin's `fiberQTL_utils.R` was inspected read-only. Its
`test_AS_topic_prop_permute_genotype()` returns a model p-value for each shuffled
dataset; `compute_empirical_pval()` then calculates
`(1 + sum(null_p <= observed_p)) / (B + 1)`. Its methylation-QTL routines
shuffle sample identities or genotype columns. Here the null instead breaks
CRE1/CRE2 fiber pairing **within each sample**, and the empirical positive-tail
p-value compares correlations using `>=`. These are different biological nulls;
we retain the existing same-fiber test and its sample restrictions.

The requested null diagnostics use **one nominal, one-sided Spearman p-value
per shuffled dataset**, with the usual t approximation (`exact = FALSE` in
`cor.test`, alternative `"greater"`). They are not 10,000 new empirical tests.
For each pair the same number of finite fibers is used for every shuffle.
Nominal p-values test zero pooled correlation; the sample-stratified null can
have a nonzero pooled correlation because sample differences are preserved.
Consequently, these histograms and QQ plots need not follow Uniform(0,1), even
when the restricted permutation procedure is working correctly. They do not
replace the empirical positive-tail p-values or their BH correction. Log-tail
probabilities are retained for finite QQ coordinates when ordinary p-values
underflow. Invalid or constant-correlation cases are omitted and counted in
panel labels. No per-shuffle tables are saved.

```{r shuffled-p-value-diagnostics, fig.height=13}
# Equivalent to the asymptotic Spearman cor.test p-value, including tied ranks.
# Shared implementation: stats_testing_functions.r.
null_p_diagnostics <- merge(
  permutation_null[, .(analysis, pair_id, pair_rank, permutation, spearman_rho)],
  permutation_statistics[, .(analysis, pair_id, n_paired_finite_fibers)],
  by = c("analysis", "pair_id"))
null_p_diagnostics[, log_p := spearman_nominal_logp(spearman_rho, n_paired_finite_fibers)]
null_p_diagnostics[, nominal_p := exp(log_p)]
for (a in analysis_sets) {
  d <- copy(null_p_diagnostics[analysis == a])
  labels <- d[, .(label = paste0(pair_id[1], "\nvalid = ", sum(!is.na(log_p)),
    "; unavailable = ", sum(is.na(log_p)))), by = .(pair_id, pair_rank)]
  setorder(labels, pair_rank)
  d[, panel := factor(pair_id, levels = labels$pair_id, labels = labels$label)]
  valid_d <- d[!is.na(log_p)]
  if (!nrow(valid_d)) next
  p <- ggplot(valid_d, aes(nominal_p)) +
    geom_histogram(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.05), colour = "white", fill = "steelblue") +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, ncol = 2, drop = FALSE) +
    labs(x = "Permutation p-value (nominal Spearman, one-sided)", y = "Frequency",
         title = paste(a, "- p-values from shuffled datasets"),
         subtitle = "Within-sample shuffles preserve sample effects; uniformity is not guaranteed") +
    theme_bw()
  print(p)
  queue_plot(p, paste0(a, "_shuffled_p_value_histograms"), height = 13)
  setorder(valid_d, pair_rank, log_p, permutation)
  valid_d[, expected := -log10((seq_len(.N) - 0.5) / .N), by = pair_id]
  # Exact rho=1 has p=0; cap only its displayed height at the machine floor.
  valid_d[, observed := -pmax(log_p, log(.Machine$double.xmin)) / log(10)]
  p <- ggplot(valid_d, aes(expected, observed)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
    geom_point(size = 0.45, alpha = 0.35) +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, ncol = 2, scales = "free", drop = FALSE) +
    labs(x = "Expected -log10(p-value)", y = "Observed -log10(shuffled nominal p-value)",
         title = paste(a, "- shuffled-dataset p-value QQ plots"),
         subtitle = "All valid draws; displayed -log10(p) capped at machine precision") +
    theme_bw()
  print(p)
  queue_plot(p, paste0(a, "_shuffled_p_value_qq"), height = 13)
}
```

The QQ plot below uses the **unadjusted empirical p-value for each observed
pair**, not BH q-values or individual shuffled correlations. Expected quantiles
are `(rank - 0.5) / n`, as in the list-input branch of Kevin's
`plots_test.R::qqplot.pvalue()`. All valid pairs are shown without thinning.
The helper's vector-input branch includes a zero expected quantile, so this
notebook constructs finite plotting positions explicitly without modifying or
sourcing Kevin's files.

With 10,000 permutations, the smallest possible empirical p-value is
`1 / 10001`; zero exceedances give that value, not zero. If all ten pairs reach
this limit, their QQ points have the same observed height. This does not resolve
how much smaller their true tail probabilities might be.

```{r empirical-p-value-qq, fig.height=6}
for (a in analysis_sets) {
  d <- copy(permutation_statistics[analysis == a & is.finite(p_positive),
    .(pair_id, p_positive)])
  if (!nrow(d)) next
  stopifnot(all(d$p_positive > 0 & d$p_positive <= 1))
  setorder(d, p_positive, pair_id)
  d[, `:=`(expected = -log10((seq_len(.N) - 0.5) / .N),
            observed = -log10(p_positive))]
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(expected, observed)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = pair_id), vjust = -0.6, size = 3, check_overlap = TRUE) +
    labs(x = "Expected -log10(p-value)", y = "Observed -log10(empirical p-value)",
         title = paste(a, "- top-10 empirical permutation p-values"),
         subtitle = paste(nrow(d), "valid pairs; selected-pair descriptive QQ plot")) +
    theme_bw()
  print(p)
  queue_plot(p, paste0(a, "_empirical_permutation_p_qq"), width = 8, height = 6)
}
```


# Final outputs

Only final processed TSV tables and PDF figures are saved in `tables/` and
`plots/` under `LCL_project/co-accessibility/co-access_v2_perm_methy_prop`.
`per_fiber_m6a_proportions`
contains every Fisher-eligible fiber, its sample/donor, FIRE state, matrix
denominators, proportions, inclusion flag, and exclusion statuses. Pooled,
FIRE-state, and donor means are separate TSVs. Final permutation statistics,
unchanged top-ten Fisher statistics, donor accessibility summaries, and
sample/pair exclusion summaries are also saved. Matrices, position lists,
permutation draws, raw audits, manifests, and settings are not saved.
Individual CRE1/CRE2 exclusion counts may overlap; `n_excluded` counts
unique fibers excluded from the paired methylation analysis.

```{r save-final-tables}
for (name in names(final_plots)) {
  p <- final_plots[[name]]
  path <- file.path(plot_dir, paste0(name, ".pdf"))
  if (file.exists(path)) stop("Refusing to overwrite ", path)
  ggsave(path, p$plot, width = p$width, height = p$height, limitsize = FALSE)
}
for (a in analysis_sets)
  write_table(selected_sets[[a]], paste0(a, "_top10_original_fisher_statistics.tsv"))
write_table(per_fiber, "per_fiber_m6a_proportions.tsv")
write_table(donor_accessibility, "donor_accessibility_observed_expected.tsv")
write_table(pooled_means, "pooled_m6a_means.tsv")
write_table(state_means, "fire_state_m6a_means.tsv")
write_table(donor_means, "donor_m6a_means.tsv")
write_table(exclusions, "m6a_exclusions_by_sample.tsv")
write_table(pair_attrition, "m6a_exclusions_by_pair.tsv")
write_table(permutation_statistics, "pooled_m6a_permutation_statistics.tsv")
cat("Final PDFs:", plot_dir, "\nFinal TSVs:", table_dir, "\n")
```
